sections.title: Snow ratio.
sections.note: Given the measured water, how far off is the snowfall? 1,197 hand-measured Sierra snow days, 2021 to 2026; each winter is scored by a model that never saw it.

sections.title: Rain or snow.
sections.note: Water wrongly called rain or snow per wet day, at 22 Tahoe snow sensors over 5,412 held-out days. The three methods are tied; calling everything snow would miss by 4.9 mm.

sections.title: Water.
sections.note: Model water against what 22 snow sensors measured, on the 2025 and 2026 winters held out in turn.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use)

sections.title: Water, Mammoth area.
sections.note: The same test against 10 snow sensors along the crest around Mammoth, on the 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters held out in turn. Mammoth Mountain and Sherwin Ridge use the Mammoth Pass sensor, Matterhorn Peak the Slide Canyon one, and Dana Plateau the Dana Meadows one; June Mountain, Carson Peak, and Mt. Whitney have no working sensor nearby and are left uncorrected.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use where a sensor is near)

sections.title: Water, Cascades.
sections.note: The same test against 10 snow sensors in the Washington Cascades and Olympics, on the 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters held out in turn. Crystal Mountain and White Pass use the curve pooled over all ten, which did better there than their own sensor's. Mt. Rainier, Mt. Baker, and Mt. St. Helens are shown their sensor but left uncorrected, since it sits far below the mountain; Glacier Peak and Mt. Adams have none.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use, except on the volcanoes)

sections.title: Rain or snow, Cascades.
sections.note: The same test at 64 snow sensors in the Washington Cascades and Olympics over 16,508 held-out days, 4,691 of them mixed. The Cascades' curve is centered at 0.75 C of wet-bulb against the Sierra's 1.25 C: more of each storm is rain. Calling everything snow would miss by 10.6 mm.

sections.title: Snow ratio, Cascades.
sections.note: The Sierra-trained ratio on 248 hand-measured snow days at 9 Washington stations, 2023 to 2026, none of which it was trained on. Refitting it with those days added did no better at a station held out (1.50 in), so the Sierra's is kept. It runs a little fluffy west of the crest and dense east of it.
rows: This site's ratio, trained in the Sierra (in use)

sections.title: Water, Tetons.
sections.note: The same test against 10 snow sensors from the Snake River's headwaters to the Gros Ventre, on the 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters held out in turn. Grand Targhee and Togwotee Pass use their own sensor and Jackson Hole and Teton Pass the Phillips Bench one; Snow King has none within reach and is left uncorrected.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use where a sensor is near)

sections.title: Rain or snow, Tetons.
sections.note: The same test at 18 snow sensors around the Tetons over 2,915 held-out days, 687 of them mixed. Nearly all of it is snow there: calling everything snow would miss by only 2.4 mm. The curve fitted there is centered at 0.75 C of wet-bulb and does no better than the Sierra's.

sections.title: Snow ratio, Tetons.
sections.note: 869 hand-measured snow days at 21 stations around Jackson, 2023 to 2026, where the snow averages 14 to 1. The Sierra-trained ratio already reads that from the cold, so adding the Teton days changes little; the one in use is scored here at stations it never saw.
rows: This site's ratio, trained in the Sierra
Trained on Sierra and Teton days together (in use)

sections.title: Water, Wasatch.
sections.note: The same test against 10 snow sensors from Timpanogos Divide to Ben Lomond Peak, on the 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters held out in turn. The models are driest in Little Cottonwood, where they deliver under half of what Snowbird's sensor measures. Snowbasin has no sensor within reach and is left uncorrected.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use where a sensor is near)

sections.title: Rain or snow, Wasatch.
sections.note: The same test at 25 snow sensors in the Wasatch over 4,125 held-out days, 1,056 of them mixed; calling everything snow would miss by 3.9 mm. The curve fitted there is centered at 0.5 C of wet-bulb, lower than the Sierra's 1.25 C.

sections.title: Snow ratio, Wasatch.
sections.note: 690 hand-measured snow days at 25 stations from Alta and Brighton down to the benches, 2023 to 2026, where the snow averages 12 to 1. The Sierra-trained ratio runs an inch too deep on them, so the one in use is trained on both, with a Wasatch day counted ten times; it is scored here at stations it never saw.
rows: This site's ratio, trained in the Sierra
Trained on Sierra and Wasatch days together (in use)

sections.title: Water, Colorado.
sections.note: The same test against 16 snow sensors, twelve along I-70 from Beaver Creek to Berthoud Pass and four in the Park Range above Steamboat, on the 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters held out in turn. The models are driest above Steamboat, where they deliver under half of what the Tower sensor measures. Breckenridge has no sensor within reach and is left uncorrected.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use where a sensor is near)

sections.title: Rain or snow, Colorado.
sections.note: The same test at 33 snow sensors in Colorado over 4,806 held-out days, 1,401 of them mixed. Nearly all of it is snow there: calling everything snow would miss by only 2.0 mm. The curve fitted there is centered at 0 C of wet-bulb and does little better than the Sierra's.

sections.title: Snow ratio, Colorado.
sections.note: 1,962 hand-measured snow days at 40 stations from Climax and Breckenridge to Steamboat Springs, 2023 to 2026, where the snow averages nearly 15 to 1. The Sierra-trained ratio runs half an inch deep on them, so the one in use is trained on both; it is scored here at stations it never saw.
rows: This site's ratio, trained in the Sierra
Trained on Sierra and Colorado days together (in use)

sections.title: Water, Okanagan.
sections.note: The same test against 10 snow stations in the Okanagan highlands. The models deliver about half of what the stations measure, and a third of it at Silver Star Mountain. SilverStar is corrected against that station; Big White, Sun Peaks and Apex have none within reach and are left uncorrected. The 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters are held out in turn.
rows: Corrected to the snow stations (in use where a station is near)

sections.title: Rain or snow, Okanagan.
sections.note: The same test at 15 snow stations in the Okanagan over 1,564 held-out days, 438 of them mixed; calling everything snow would miss by 3.1 mm. The curve fitted there is centered at 0.25 C of wet-bulb, against the Sierra's 1.25 C.

sections.title: Water, BC Coast.
sections.note: The same test against 11 snow stations from the North Shore to Bralorne and Vancouver Island. The models are closer here, but deliver 70% of what Palisade Lake measures above Grouse, which is corrected against it. Nothing with a record is within reach of Whistler, Cypress, Mt. Seymour or Mt. Washington, which are left uncorrected. The 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters are held out in turn.
rows: Corrected to the snow stations (in use where a station is near)

sections.title: Rain or snow, BC Coast.
sections.note: The same test at 17 snow stations in the south Coast Mountains over 3,412 held-out days, 1,045 of them mixed; calling everything snow would miss by 10.6 mm. The curve fitted there is centered at 0.25 C of wet-bulb, against the Sierra's 1.25 C.
rows: The BC Coast's wet-bulb curve (in use)

sections.title: Water, Powder Highway.
sections.note: The same test against 9 snow stations in the Selkirks and Monashees. Revelstoke is corrected against Mount Revelstoke's station, where the models deliver 56%, and Rogers Pass against the station in the valley below it; RED Mountain, Whitewater and Kootenay Pass have none within reach and are left uncorrected. The 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters are held out in turn.
rows: Corrected to the snow stations (in use where a station is near)

sections.title: Rain or snow, Powder Highway.
sections.note: The same test at 18 snow stations in the Selkirks and Monashees over 2,588 held-out days, 567 of them mixed; calling everything snow would miss by 2.6 mm. The curve fitted there is centered at 0.75 C of wet-bulb, against the Sierra's 1.25 C.
rows: The Powder Highway's wet-bulb curve (in use)

sections.title: Water, East Kootenays.
sections.note: The same test against 6 snow stations in the Purcells and on the Rockies' west slope. Fernie is corrected against Morrissey Ridge; Kicking Horse, Panorama and Kimberley have no station within reach and are left uncorrected. The 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters are held out in turn.
rows: Corrected to the snow stations (in use where a station is near)

sections.title: Rain or snow, East Kootenays.
sections.note: The same test at 15 snow stations in the Purcells and the Rockies' west slope over 1,542 held-out days, 364 of them mixed; calling everything snow would miss by 2.7 mm. The curve fitted there is centered at 0.25 C of wet-bulb, against the Sierra's 1.25 C.
rows: The East Kootenays' wet-bulb curve (in use)

sections.title: Water, Canadian Rockies.
sections.note: The same test against 4 snow stations on the British Columbia side of the divide, which is all that has a record: Alberta publishes five days of readings. Bow Summit is corrected against Wildcat Creek; the mountains in Alberta are left uncorrected. The 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters are held out in turn.
rows: Corrected to the snow stations (in use where a station is near)

sections.title: Rain or snow, Canadian Rockies.
sections.note: The same test at 12 snow stations in the Rockies and the Columbias beside them over 2,091 held-out days, 427 of them mixed; calling everything snow would miss by 2.7 mm. The curve fitted there is centered at 0.25 C of wet-bulb, against the Sierra's 1.25 C.
rows: The Canadian Rockies' wet-bulb curve (in use)
